newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp. drops hostile bid for Loewen.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp. drops hostile bid for Loewen.

text.p: North America's largest funeral home operator, Service Corp. International, said in a surprise announcement Tuesday that it was dropping its $2.9 billion hostile bid for Canadian archrival Loewen Group Inc.

Houston-based Service Corp. cited Loewen's recent acquisition programme, costs associated with Loewen's executive severance packages and uncertainties about divestitures that might be required to complete the transaction.
Loewen, based in Vancouver, British Columbia, is Service Corp.'s biggest rival. The company has survived several near-death experiences over the past year, including a brush with bankruptcy.

"The cumulative effect of actions taken by Loewen since our offer was announced, and the disclosure of details related to certain of Loewen's other transactions, have adversely impacted SCI's view of Loewen's value to SCI shareholders," Service Corp. Chairman R.L. Waltrip said in a statement released after stock markets closed.
"Consequently, rather than reducing our offer, SCI has decided not to pursue the acquisition of Loewen at this time."

Loewen said last month that the Federal Trade Commission, the Canadian Competition Bureau and officials in several U.S. states had launched investigations into the potential antitrust implications of a deal.
Loewen said it was surprised by Service Corp.'s decision to drop the takeover effort. "We are obviously very pleased," a company spokesman said in a telephone interview.
Loewen has said it preferred to remain independent and had resisted the Service Corp. offer.
Service's announcement also stunned investors. "This has caught everyone by surprise," said one trader.
Analysts said any elation felt by Loewen was likely to be tempered by a swift drop in the company's stock price Wednesday.

Analysts and arbitragers predicted the stock, which soared in September on the first news of Service Corp.'s bid, would drop 5 percent to 15 percent. Loewen stock closed Tuesday at $40.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, up 12.5 cents.
"I would expect Loewen stock to move back. Thirty-seven dollars would probably be reasonable but it might go back as low as $34," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
One arbitrageur said he anticipated a drop of $5 a share or so in Loewen's shares early Wednesday.

Analysts said that Loewen's stock should attract buying interest after an initial sell-off. The extent of the losses may be blunted because most investors who bought the stock purely for takeover interest have already sold their shares. Service had been waiting since October for regulatory approval of its offer and many traders had anticipated a long wait.
Service Corp. had 2,864 funeral service locations, 335 cemeteries and 147 crematoria worldwide as of Sept. 30. It provides funeral and cemetery services in North America, Europe and the Pacific Rim.

Loewen is the second largest funeral home and cemetery operator in North America after Service. It owns about 951 funeral homes and 299 cemeteries in the United States and Canada with about 90 percent of its revenue coming from U.S. operations.
